title: How Advertisers Make Us Spend Money

blanks.sentence: Promotion by a famous person is called a _____.
People often follow those they see as _____ when they are unsure.
This quick decision aid is described as a _____.
This pattern of relying on trusted figures begins from an _____.
Parents and teachers help people learn and _____ of the world.
Ordering from a person may make customers _____.
Touchscreens give customers _____ to consider products and linked items.
Suggestions such as adding extra items are part of an _____ strategy.
This can raise typical basket spend by _____.
The TV series relied on people learning by _____ others.

multipleChoice.question: What is meant by a celebrity endorsement in this context?
options: A customer reviewing a product after buying it.
A famous or liked person promoting a product.
A shop reducing the price of a product.
A scientist testing whether a product works.

multipleChoice.question: Why can endorsements influence people when they are unsure?
options: They remove all risk from the purchase.
They force people to copy their parents.
They provide detailed technical comparisons.
They offer a quick cue from someone trusted.

multipleChoice.question: What does the speaker mean by a 'mental shortcut'?
options: A way to make quick decisions under uncertainty.
A method for memorising advertisements.
A habit of buying the cheapest product.
A plan to avoid buying unnecessary items.

multipleChoice.question: Why are parents, teachers, dentists and athletes mentioned?
options: To show that only experts can sell products.
To argue that childhood habits disappear in adulthood.
To illustrate how trusted figures can guide behaviour.
To compare education with professional sport.

multipleChoice.question: Why may customers refuse extra food when ordering from a human server?
options: They cannot see the product clearly.
They may worry about being judged.
They have no time to make a choice.
They are not allowed to change orders.

multipleChoice.question: What advantage do touchscreen ordering machines give customers?
options: They prevent companies from upselling.
They make customers speak to staff more often.
They hide linked products from the customer.
They allow more time to view products and related items.

multipleChoice.question: What is the likely commercial effect of touchscreens in fast-food restaurants?
options: Customers tend to spend more per transaction.
Customers usually buy fewer linked products.
Restaurants stop suggesting extra items.
Basket spend becomes impossible to measure.

multipleChoice.question: Why did the World Food Programme choose a TV series?
options: To avoid showing any human behaviour.
To replace food assistance with entertainment.
To use stories creatively so viewers could recognise themselves.
To provide technical training for restaurant staff.

multipleChoice.question: According to Takwa, how do people learn and change in this project?
options: By observing and copying behaviours and reactions.
By receiving direct financial rewards.
By reading scientific papers in detail.
By being ordered to eat together.

multipleChoice.question: What does the TV programme example show about behavioural science?
options: It is only useful for selling fast food.
It works only when people are unaware of it.
It depends entirely on celebrity advertising.
It can encourage social behaviour by providing models to copy.
